post.description:
Reads the file as bytes. **An Excel workbook** (ADR-0184) is opened only after its parts, as its own directory declares them, are checked to unpack to at most 25 MiB in at most 1,000 parts (`ASSET_TOO_LARGE`, 413, otherwise), and its *Data* sheet is read, at most 10,000 rows (`format: 'xlsx'`). **A CSV** is read as UTF-8, or Windows-1252 when it is not valid UTF-8, with a comma, semicolon or tab delimiter. Either way the header is matched column by column against the KPM’s template — `[KODE]`, then the ID label, the EN label and the aliases (ADR-0214 §5) — and `notes` say what the file lacks or carries that is not stored. **Writes nothing.** Answers every data row against the roster and what is stored: `refused` with its reason, `held` for a code no member holds under the template’s `unknownAgent: flag`, else `ready`, its cells — one per `columns` entry — each `new`, `changed`, `unchanged`, `not_provided` or `refused`. A blank cell is not provided and would change nothing (ADR-0051). `UPLOAD_TEMPLATE_MISMATCH` (422) for a file with no Agent Code column, no column read, or two headers on one kode; `UPLOAD_MALFORMED_CSV` (422); `ASSET_TOO_LARGE` (413) above 1 MiB.

**Requires `data_upload:upload_and_preview`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

**Requires `data_upload:commit_import`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

Answers the queue. `startFrom` is *Mulai dari* (ADR-0213 §3), offered when the company has no template: absent, the company's default template, or the built-in default where it has none.

post.description:
The only way an office comes into existence — there is no self-service path (ADR-0005). Seeds the per-office settings every prototype screen hardcodes, and its configuration from `startFrom` (ADR-0115): one of the company's active templates, the Template library's (`templateLibrary`, ADR-0164), or empty — the company's default template when absent. `kind: 'defaults'` is refused 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, `details.field: 'startFrom.kind'`: the Template's Default template holds the AgencyBoost defaults (ADR-0168 §2). There is no fallback: a kind the source holds none of is empty in the office, and every office has the three cascade activity types. The whole source is checked before the office is written, so a refusal (400, naming what is broken; 404 for a template that is not the company's; 409 TEMPLATE_RUNG_UNKNOWN for a library template naming a role the company's ladder lacks) leaves nothing behind. The Template library itself holds no office: 409 COMPANY_IS_TEMPLATE_LIBRARY. **`owner`** (ADR-0212 §1, §2; *Pemilik KPM*): made the Owner as one unit with the KPM — checked before anything is written as `PATCH /admin/tenants/:id/owner` checks one (`409 TENANT_COMPANY_MISMATCH`, `409 AUTH_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`; for an email nobody holds `agentCode` required, `400`, and free, `409 AGENT_CODE_TAKEN`), and a failure after the KPM is written undoes it. With no `email`, no account: `pendingOwner`, *Belum diundang*. `sendInvitation` (default `true`) emails the Owner a one-time link to choose a password; `invitationSent` says whether it went. A code taken in the company is `409 TENANT_CODE_TAKEN`: *"Kode 0417 sudah dipakai KPM lain di Prudential: …"*.

**Requires `kpm:create`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

Defaults to the caller's own tenant. A Super Admin has no tenant, so their default is the platform-level log — provisioning, companies, templates, products, support sessions — and `kpmId` narrows it to one office. Anyone else is pinned to their own office whatever they pass. Within that reach `companyId`, `action`, `actorUserId`, `from` and `to` narrow it, together. Newest first, and **grouped on the server**: consecutive rows with the same actor, action and target within 10 minutes of the group's newest (inclusive) are one item carrying `count` and `oldestAt`. At most 50 items a page, never a group split across two; `page.nextCursor` asks for the next, and is null on the last. The first page (no `cursor`) carries `facets`, the actions and actors within the reach. **In words** (SA UI-016): each item carries `actionLabel` and `targetKind` in the reader's language and `targetLabel`, the target's name — *"Prudential template · Aktivitas & rasio"*, *"PRUProsper"*, *"KPM 0417 · Bandung"* — and `facets.actionLabels` the chip's words. A leader note's rows about the reader are dropped before grouping (ADR-0073). A query field that is not a string, or not its shape, is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming it.

**Requires `audit_log:read`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

post.description:
What the office’s agents read — its newest published configuration snapshot (activity types, ratios, both lead pipelines, the training agents are offered, event types and the capability ladder without archived rows), its newest published activation checklist, and each offered module’s content — becomes a new template of `companyId`: the office’s own company or another. Never the Owner’s unpublished draft, anything archived, or any member, log or lead. What archiving left behind is dropped and listed in `dropped`, never refused: an archived activity type out of a ratio (the ratio left out if a side counts nothing else), a stage’s archived milestones (the stage left out if it requires nothing else), a checklist item’s link to a module no longer offered (kept as a manual item). Each kind it holds is published as version 1; a kind it holds nothing of is left empty. The office’s own training files are duplicated into the company’s assets, and into another company every file is; links are copied as links. 400 when the settings would produce a broken office; 409 TEMPLATE_RUNG_UNKNOWN `{ codes }` into another company whose ladder lacks a rung they name; 409 TEMPLATE_NAME_TAKEN; 409 ASSET_NOT_CONFIRMED for a file that never finished uploading; 404 for an unknown office or company; 403 PERM_DENIED, here and in the service, to anybody without `company_template:write`. Every check runs before any write. Audited once, naming the office, the destination and what was dropped.

**Requires `company_template:write`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

The settings screens stage every edit and send one request. **Validated entirely before anything is written**, so a refusal leaves the office exactly as it was, and so a `type.create` can name a section a `category.create` makes earlier in the same batch. Every change to an existing row carries the `version` the screen read: a row that moved on refuses the whole batch with `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`, naming what changed, rather than letting the second of two admins erase the first. Returns the working copy as it now stands — publishing is still a separate act. The summary tiles (ADR-0064) are checked against the state the **whole batch** leaves, so a tile of two sections is renamed in one request: two sections of one tile left with different labels is `422 CONFIG_SUMMARY_GROUP_LABEL_MISMATCH`, and a shared tile whose code a section outside it carries is `422 CONFIG_SUMMARY_GROUP_CODE_TAKEN`.

**Requires `tenant_config:write`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

Everything but the identity and the lifecycle. There is no `code` here — it never changes — and no `lifecycle`, which moves through the three routes below. `expectedVersion`, when sent, must be the version read, or `409 VERSION_CONFLICT` and nothing is written. The attack plan's text fields and `differentiator` keep their line breaks; the other text fields are one line. A rider's `attachesTo` must name this company's active base products (`400`), and a kind does not change under an attachment (`409 PRODUCT_KIND_IN_USE`, ADR-0209 §2).

**Requires `product_catalog:crud`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

get.description:
The product the office keeps on, still issued and serving the brief’s need, that fits the brief best — an eligible age band scores 1 and an eligible budget band 2, highest first, ties in the company’s order, with no minimum — with its verdict (*Good fit* when both bands match, else *Check fit* and which bands it is outside), its words, and the brief’s other matches in score order, four of them and a count of the rest. `product: null` when nothing the office keeps on serves the need. Every member of the office — the Owner and the Admin through their field view, an AB, an AAB and an Agent — and a support session acting as one. A Super Admin outside a support session belongs to no office and is refused `403 TENANT_NO_MEMBERSHIP`.

**Requires `product_catalog:read`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

put.description:
An upsert: the whole day is sent, and a code left out counts as zero. Free within the current calendar month plus the office’s grace window; **a future day is refused**, and a day past its window is refused with a pointer at the correction route (ADR-0042).

**Codes are checked against the office’s published configuration**, the one the screen shows: a type archived since the last publish still saves, one created since is refused by name until it is published, and one in a section your rung is not shown is `ACTIVITY_TYPE_NOT_APPLICABLE`.

**There is no `membershipId` parameter.** No role may log on another person’s behalf, and a route with no subject to pass is a stronger guarantee than a check somebody has to remember.

**Requires `activity_log:create`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

info.title: AgencyBoost API
info.description:
Multi-tenant SaaS for insurance agency offices (KPM).

Every failure uses one envelope — `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }` — and every `code` has a row in `docs/02-specs/api/error-catalog.md`. **Branch on the code, never on the message.**

A resource in another tenant answers `404`, not `403`: a `403` would confirm the id exists.

**Every sentence is in the request's language** — a refusal's `message`, its `details.violations`, a notice: `Accept-Language` (`id` or `en`, exactly), else the signed-in person's saved language, else Bahasa Indonesia, the default since 2026-10-29 (`docs/02-specs/api/conventions.md`). `code` and every other detail are the same in both.

firstMonth.description: The office’s first month, `YYYY-MM`, in its zone: the earliest `month` there is, and its year the earliest `year`.

thisMonth.description: The office’s current month, `YYYY-MM`: the latest there is.

currentMonth.description: `month` is the current month: its days run to today, and the pace is said. Otherwise it is read whole, with no pace.

currentYear.description: `year` is the current year: its days run to today. Otherwise it is read whole, to 31 December.

set.description: A goal has been saved for the year. The defaults a first-time reader sees are not one.

gapMinor.description: *Sisa*: the whole target — `APE_GAP_TO_TARGET` at an APE of 0. IDR minor units.

policiesNeeded.description: `POLICIES_NEEDED` at an APE of 0; `null` without a case size.

membershipId.description: The membership: the person in this agency, never their account.
The membership: the person in this agency, never their account.

provenance.description: The carrier’s file, a correction by hand, or a figure **typed in the app, not uploaded** — by the member, or by whoever coaches them (`typedBy`).

correctedBy.description: Who corrected the figure by hand — an owner or administrator at the month table, or a leader on the Unit Dashboard. `null` for the file’s figure and the agent’s own, and when they can no longer be named.

correctedAt.description: When, for a correction by hand. ISO.

typedBy.description: Who typed a `self_reported` figure, **when it was not the member** — a coach (S2). Absent when the member typed it, and on every other source.

targetMinor.description: IDR minor units. `null` without a goal.

actualMinor.description: `null` when nothing is held yet — not zero.

attainmentPct.description: `APE_ATTAINMENT_PCT`, capped at 999. `null` without a target or an actual.

production.description: `official`: the office’s file, imported or corrected. `estimate`: the member’s own figure, typed on Goal Settings or the Summary — *perkiraan Anda* (a coach’s typing too, ADR-0183); the year only. `none`: nothing yet.

withoutProduction.description: With `production: none` and a target above 0 not yet met, the helpers counting what was achieved as 0 (UI-157 item 2), which the screen marks *(belum ada data produksi)*; `null` otherwise.

source.description: Where this month’s APE came from; `null` until the file for the month arrives.

targetMinor.description: IDR minor units. `null` without a goal.

actualMinor.description: `null` when nothing is held yet — not zero.

attainmentPct.description: `APE_ATTAINMENT_PCT`, capped at 999. `null` without a target or an actual.

production.description: `official`: the office’s file, imported or corrected. `estimate`: the member’s own figure, typed on Goal Settings or the Summary — *perkiraan Anda* (a coach’s typing too, ADR-0183); the year only. `none`: nothing yet.

withoutProduction.description: With `production: none` and a target above 0 not yet met, the helpers counting what was achieved as 0 (UI-157 item 2), which the screen marks *(belum ada data produksi)*; `null` otherwise.

source.description: The office’s year to date, or the agent’s own figure.

uploadedOn.description: The office’s day its year-to-date figure was written — the correction’s, or the year’s latest import — after the estimate: *Diganti data produksi resmi (diunggah 5 Des)*.

closingTarget.description: *M*: this month’s closing target — the closings chip’s.

closingsLast30Days.description: *N*, `CLOSINGS_LAST_30_DAYS`: the goal’s closing code over the last 30 days, today included, in the office’s calendar.

weeksLeft.description: *W*: days left today included, over 7, rounded up — never zero.

policiesNeeded.description: `POLICIES_NEEDED` for the month: this month’s APE gap over the case size, rounded up — the whole target’s until the month’s file lands; 0 once the target is reached.

neededPerWeek.description: *K*, `CLOSINGS_NEEDED_PER_WEEK`: the policies still needed over the weeks left, rounded up.

targetMet.description: This month’s APE target, or the year’s, is reached: the green sentence instead of the danger box.

source.description: Every count of policies on the page — the *Submission polis* chips and the pace sentence’s *closing N* — is the member’s activity log. APE, the gap and *Polis yang dibutuhkan* are the production upload’s (`monthly.source`, `yearly.source`). The screen says which (UI-052).

codes.description: The codes the office binds to *Submission polis*, counted.

month.description: The office’s day its latest production file for `month` was uploaded, in its calendar; `null` while there is none.

year.description: The office’s day its latest production file of any month of `year`, up to `month`, was uploaded; `null` while there is none.

code.description: The first code the office binds to this role (its activity binding).

codes.description: Every code the office binds to this role; `logged` is their sum, so a replaced activity keeps counting.

logged.description: Logged over the period, every bound code summed, archived types included.

target.description: `SUMMARY_ACTIVITY_TARGET`. `null` without an APE target; 0 when the month needs nothing more — met, not unmeasured.

attainmentPct.description: `ACTIVITY_TARGET_ATTAINMENT_PCT`, capped at 999; `null` on a zero or missing target.

code.description: The summary tile's group code (ADR-0064), or the section's own code when it has a tile of its own.

label.description: The group's label, or the section's own.

total.description: `ACTIVITY_TOTAL_BY_CATEGORY` over the period, summed over the tile's sections; the rows add up to it.

targets.description: Leads contacted, appointments, closings — in that order. The year’s are the cascade on what the year still needs, so its closings target is `yearly.policiesNeeded` (UI-052).

total.description: *n aktivitas*: the sum of the rows below — `targets` and every row of `sections`, each code once (UI-052).

sections.description: One per summary tile the reader is shown (ADR-0064) whose sections hold none of the three codes above.

monthly.description: This calendar month, against the cascade on `MONTHLY_APE_TARGET`.

yearly.description: The year to date, against the cascade on the annual target.

statusLabel.description: The office’s name for the stage, archived stages included.

thisMonth.description: Promised for the office’s current month.

flags.description: As the Leads screen derives them (`leadFlags`).

overdueDays.description: Whole days in the office’s zone; `null` unless overdue.

rows.description: The nearest `SUMMARY.LEADS_SHOWN` (10), nearest next action first, undated last.

total.description: Every open lead of the reader’s own.

unitOpen.description: The open leads of everybody else the reader’s `lead:read` reaches — what Leads Management lists them besides their own. Counted on the reader’s own summary while `total` is 0; 0 otherwise.

rule.description: The rule that fired — the card names it (ADR-0060).

kind.description: *What to do next*, or *How you can improve your performance*.

facts.description: What the rule read. NOTHING_LOGGED: `windowDays`, `lastLoggedOn`. BEHIND_PACE: `closingsLast30Days`, `closingTarget`, `neededPerWeek`, `weeksLeft`. LEAD_OVERDUE: `leadId`, `name`, `overdueDays`, `others`. LEAD_NEGLECTED: `leadId`, `name`, `others`. RATIO_BELOW, RATIO_STRENGTH: `code`, `label`, `value`, `benchmark`, `displayUnit`.

year.description: The year *Yearly* is about: this one, or the one asked for.

month.description: The month *Monthly* is about: this one, the one asked for, or the December of a closed year asked for.

monthly.description: *Monthly* (ADR-0056): `MONTHLY_APE_TARGET` — fixed against this month’s own figure — against this month’s uploaded APE.

yearly.description: *Yearly*: the annual target against the year to date.

estimateReplaced.description: The office’s year-to-date figure, written after it, replaced a typed estimate the plan still stores (UI-157 item 4, ADR-0195 §3); `null` when nothing was replaced.

pace.description: The pace sentence (ADR-0109); `null` without a goal, and for a month that has ended (ADR-0161).

policies.description: Where every count of policies on the page comes from: the activity log (UI-052).

uploadedOn.description: The day the page’s APE is valid for — the latest production upload of the month, and of the year (UI-054).

activity.description: *Your sales activity targets* and the other sections.

leads.description: *Leads that need you*: the reader’s own open leads.

insights.description: The insight cards: the rules that fired, in their fixed priority, at most four.

code.description: A stable code from `docs/02-specs/api/error-catalog.md`. Branch on this, never on the message.

message.example: You do not have permission to do that.
message.description: Written for a person, in the request's language: `Accept-Language` (`id` or `en`), else the signed-in person's saved language, else Bahasa Indonesia, the default since 2026-10-29. Wording may change; the code will not.

details.description: What is specific to this failure — the permission that was missing, the field that was wrong, the code already taken.

requestId.description: On every response and in every log line. Quote it to support.

from.description: The first of the 7 days, the office’s calendar.

to.description: The office’s today, the last of the 7.

count.description: *Aktivitas 7 hari*: every count the person logged over the 7 days — the coaching session’s Activity card.

actualMinor.description: *Produksi tahun ini*, IDR sen: the office’s year to date for the member — **never their own estimate**. `null` while the office holds none (*Belum diunggah*).

targetMinor.description: The year’s goal, IDR sen; `null` while no goal is saved (*no goal*).

attainmentPct.description: *n% dari goal* (`APE_ATTAINMENT_PCT`, capped for display); `null` without a goal or an official figure.

goalSet.description: A goal is saved for the year. An unsaved default measures nobody.

date.description: The day of their latest 1:1 as coachee, finalized at least once.

month.description: The office’s calendar month the closings are counted in.

open.description: *Leads*: their open sales leads, the Unit Dashboard row’s *Leads penjualan*.

closing.description: *n closing*: their sales leads that first reached *Paid and issued* this month, the row’s *Closing*.

today.description: The office’s day the figures are as of.

products.description: The item names of the live proposal updated last that has a product, as the proposal shows them, in order. Empty when every live proposal of the lead is still empty.

count.description: The lead’s live proposals, drafts included.

ownerMembershipId.description: The membership whose lead it is, never a user id.

thisMonth.description: **Derived**: is there a commitment for the office’s current month? Nothing clears it, so it cannot be left true for an agent who has not opened the app since March.

committedMonths.description: Every month this lead was promised for, oldest first, in the office’s timezone. The archive behind *did they do what they said* — written when the promise is made rather than swept somewhere when the month ends.

closedThisMonth.description: **Derived** (UI-153 item 5): marked *Berhasil* inside the office’s current month. With `thisMonth` it is the avatar’s badge — yellow ✓ switched on and not closed, green ✓ switched on and closed this month — and it clears on the 1st with the switch.

age.description: **The client's age at the next birthday, today** (*Umur ulang tahun berikutnya*; ADR-0224 §2): the age written plus the whole years since `ageRecordedOn`, on the office's calendar — one more on each anniversary, at 00:00 WIB. `null` when none was given. Read by whoever reads the lead.

ageRecordedOn.description: The office's day the age was last written, `YYYY-MM-DD`; `null` with it. Set by the server only.

gender.description: *Laki-laki* or *Perempuan* (ADR-0224 §1), or `null`. Printed nowhere, and decides no figure.

version.description: What a later write pins, so two people cannot overwrite each other.

flags.description: Computed on read, never stored — a stored flag is one that is wrong at midnight. A closed lead carries none. **A commitment for this month does not suppress them**, unlike the prototype, which shows only the green chip on a lead that is also two weeks overdue.

lastEditedBy.description: Who last changed this lead, when that was not the agent whose lead it is (ADR-0044) — `null` otherwise. A proxy edit is recognisable by `updatedBy` differing from `ownerMembershipId`: two columns, so no flag is needed.

overdueDays.description: How late, in the office’s own calendar days — `null` unless `flags` carries `overdue`. Beside `flags` rather than inside it: `flags` is what the list filters on, and a filter key carrying a number is one nobody can match against.

proposals.description: How many live proposals the lead has, and the latest’s products — the card’s *"PRUWell Medical +1"*. **`null` on a lead with none, and on every lead that is not yours**: a leader reads a downline’s lead, never what was proposed on it.

total.description: Matching the filter, not on this page.

kind.description: `stage`: a move. `proposal`: *"Proposal dibuat · …"*, derived.

at.description: A move’s time, or the proposal’s first *Simpan PDF*.

fromStatusCode.description: `stage` only. `null` on the lead’s first move.

toStatusCode.description: `stage` only. A code; the office names it.

proposalId.description: `proposal` only: the proposal to open, or `null` once it is deleted — the note stays, its link goes.

products.description: `proposal` only: its item names when first saved, in order.

ownerMembershipId.description: The membership whose lead it is, never a user id.

thisMonth.description: **Derived**: is there a commitment for the office’s current month? Nothing clears it, so it cannot be left true for an agent who has not opened the app since March.

committedMonths.description: Every month this lead was promised for, oldest first, in the office’s timezone. The archive behind *did they do what they said* — written when the promise is made rather than swept somewhere when the month ends.

closedThisMonth.description: **Derived** (UI-153 item 5): marked *Berhasil* inside the office’s current month. With `thisMonth` it is the avatar’s badge — yellow ✓ switched on and not closed, green ✓ switched on and closed this month — and it clears on the 1st with the switch.

Read by whoever reads the lead.

gender.description: *Laki-laki* or *Perempuan* (ADR-0224 §1), or `null`. Printed nowhere, and decides no figure.

version.description: What a later write pins, so two people cannot overwrite each other.

lastEditedBy.description: Who last changed this lead, when that was not the agent whose lead it is (ADR-0044) — `null` otherwise. A proxy edit is recognisable by `updatedBy` differing from `ownerMembershipId`: two columns, so no flag is needed.

overdueDays.description: How late, in the office’s own calendar days — `null` unless `flags` carries `overdue`. Beside `flags` rather than inside it: `flags` is what the list filters on, and a filter key carrying a number is one nobody can match against.

proposals.description: How many live proposals the lead has, and the latest’s products — the card’s *"PRUWell Medical +1"*. **`null` on a lead with none, and on every lead that is not yours**: a leader reads a downline’s lead, never what was proposed on it.

history.description: Every move along its ladder, oldest first. Append-only: a reopen or a type change adds none. On your own lead, the proposals ever saved as a PDF are interleaved by date (`kind: 'proposal'`).

type.description: Null until the agent picks a ladder.

contact.description: Both optional, both clearable, sent as a pair. **No lawful basis is asked for since 2026-10-07** (ADR-0108 §1): `lawfulBasis` is no longer a field, and a body carrying it is refused with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` like any other unknown field.

thisMonth.description: The agent’s own commitment for the month.

age.description: **The client's age at the next birthday** (*Umur ulang tahun berikutnya*; ADR-0224 §3): a whole number from 1 to 100, or `null` to clear it. Outside the bounds it is `422 LEAD_AGE_OUT_OF_RANGE` with `details: { min, max }`; not a whole number, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`. The server records today as `ageRecordedOn` — **only when the age differs from the one the lead reads today**, so saving the age shown moves nothing. **No `birthDate`** is taken (minimisation, §6): a body carrying one, or `ageRecordedOn`, is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` as any unknown field is.

ids.description: Every one of your open leads, once each, top first. A closed or deleted lead, somebody else’s, another office’s, a repeat or one left out is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, and nothing is written.
Your open leads’ ids, in the order now saved.

type.description: Null until the agent picks a ladder.

contact.description: Both optional, both clearable, sent as a pair. **No lawful basis is asked for since 2026-10-07** (ADR-0108 §1): `lawfulBasis` is no longer a field, and a body carrying it is refused with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` like any other unknown field.

thisMonth.description: The agent’s own commitment for the month.

age.description: **The client's age at the next birthday** (*Umur ulang tahun berikutnya*; ADR-0224 §3): a whole number from 1 to 100, or `null` to clear it. Outside the bounds it is `422 LEAD_AGE_OUT_OF_RANGE` with `details: { min, max }`; not a whole number, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`. The server records today as `ageRecordedOn` — **only when the age differs from the one the lead reads today**, so saving the age shown moves nothing. **No `birthDate`** is taken (minimisation, §6): a body carrying one, or `ageRecordedOn`, is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` as any unknown field is.

version.description: The `version` this patch was written against. Refused with `409 VERSION_CONFLICT` if the lead has moved on — two people in one 1-on-1 on two devices is the realistic case. Optional for the lead’s owner; **required of anybody else**, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` without it.
The version this write was read at. Optional for the lead’s owner; required of anybody else.

statusCode.description: Any **active** stage of this lead’s own ladder, at any time (ADR-0045). Refused for the other pipeline’s stages, for an archived one, and for a lead that is already closed.

version.description: The version this write was read at. Optional for the lead’s owner; required of anybody else.

outcome.description: `won` needs the stage that closes the pipeline; `lost` needs nothing; `null` reopens. Reopening appends no transition — the lead has not moved.

done.description: `true` ticks the next action done; `false` puts the one last ticked back.

version.description: The version the lead was read at.

membershipId.description: The membership: the person in this office, never their account.

name.description: `null` when they can no longer be named.

minor.description: The APE `projected` is computed from, in IDR minor units.

provenance.description: The carrier’s file, a correction by hand, or a figure **typed in the app, not uploaded** — by the member, or by whoever coaches them (ADR-0183; `typedBy`). On the member’s own plan **the newer of the typed figure and the office’s year to date** (ADR-0230 §6): a figure typed after the office last wrote the year, until an import or a correction written after it. On a leader’s or the office’s reads the office’s figure whenever it holds one.

month.description: The month whose year-to-date figure it is; `null` for the agent’s own.

typedBy.description: Who typed a `self_reported` figure, **when it was not the member** — a coach (S2). Absent when the member typed it, and on the office’s own figure.

minor.description: The office’s year to date for the plan’s year, in IDR minor units.

provenance.description: The carrier’s file, or a correction by hand.

month.description: The latest month the year to date reads: *⚡ Otomatis · per Okt 2026*.

policiesPerWeek.description: Steps 3 and 5’s `≈ n/week`: `policiesPerMonth` ÷ 4.33 to **one decimal**, a whole figure whole — `1.4` for six a month (ADR-0160 §5).

appointmentsPerWeek.description: The `≈ n/week` sub-line: ÷ 4.33, rounded up, a whole count.

leadsPerWeek.description: The `≈ n/week` sub-line: ÷ 4.33, rounded up, a whole count.

targetMet.description: The annual target is reached, so every figure above is zero (ADR-0047). The screen replaces the cascade with a sentence rather than printing *contact 0 leads* to the best producer in the office.

leadToAppointmentRate.description: `MEASURED_LEAD_TO_APPOINTMENT_RATE` (ADR-0055): the goal’s appointments code ÷ its leads code, as a proportion. **`null` is not enough data** — nothing to divide by — never 0.

closingRate.description: `MEASURED_CLOSING_RATE` (ADR-0055): the goal’s closings code ÷ its appointments code. `null` is not enough data.

monthsLeft.description: The divisor **in force**, derived on every read from the office’s calendar unless the agent overrode it. Never served from storage: a plan saved in January would otherwise still claim eleven months left in October (client PRD §17).

monthsLeftIsOverride.description: Whether the figure above is the agent’s own choice or the office’s calendar.

apeAchievedMinor.description: The typed figure — the agent’s, or a coach’s while the office held none (ADR-0183) — kept, and used while it is newer than the office’s year to date (ADR-0230 §6). 0 is nothing typed.

achieved.description: The figure the plan is measured against, and whose it is.

official.description: **The office’s own year to date for the year, whichever figure is in force** (ADR-0230 §4): what Goal Settings prefills as *⚡ Otomatis · per {month}* and puts back with *Pakai otomatis*. `null` while the office holds none.

leadsToApptPct.description: *Appointment to Sales meeting*, a percentage. Unsaved, the office’s *Set appointment to meeting* benchmark, or 30 (ADR-0160 §3).

closingRatePct.description: *Closing rate*, a percentage. Unsaved, the office’s *Selling success rate* benchmark, or 30 (ADR-0160 §3).

snapshot.description: What was agreed, frozen at save time. **Never a display source** — `projected` is what a screen renders, because `monthsLeft` shrinks every day.

projected.description: What the inputs mean **today**, recomputed on every read. `null` when the stored inputs cannot produce a plan: a write refuses that by name, and a read must not, or a goal saved before the rule would lock its agent out of the screen that could fix it.

cascadeMapping.description: Activity **codes**, never positions: the first code of each role in the office’s binding when the plan was first saved, kept as its record and never rewritten. Nothing counts from it — see `cascadeBinding`.

cascadeBinding.description: What the three columns count today: the office’s activity binding, each role a list of codes, summed. The *Activity #n* chips are drawn from it.

measured.description: Your own conversion rates over the last 30 days, over the office’s cascade binding — printed under the assumptions they measure. Read only: nothing is filled in (ADR-0048, ADR-0055). **`null` on anybody else’s plan**: reading or saving somebody else’s goal answers no rate from their log.

apeAchievedTypedAt.description: When `apeAchievedMinor` last changed — a save that changed it, or the member’s own estimate (ADR-0195 §3). `null` on a plan from before it was recorded, and on the office’s defaults.

savedByMembershipId.description: Who saved it. Differing from the goal’s own membership is a leader’s goal-setting — two columns, no flag (ADR-0046).

mode.description: Which entry mode produced the annual target.

savingsTargetMinor.description: IDR sen. Kept in either mode, so switching back is lossless.

commissionRatePct.description: Per cent. `12.5` is twelve and a half — decimals survive (I-108).

monthsLeft.description: The cascade’s divisor. Defaulted per office, and overridable.

apeAchievedMinor.description: IDR sen. The typed figure. **On your own plan it is stored and typed now, also over the office’s figure** (ADR-0230): the newer of it and the office’s year to date is the one your screens measure against, until an import or a correction written after it. **`null` clears it** — *Pakai otomatis*, saved — and the office’s figure is read again (0 is nothing typed). On a save of somebody else’s plan (`for`) it is stored while the office holds no figure for them, and ignored — their stored figure kept — once it holds one (ADR-0183, partly reversing ADR-0075). **Optional, and absent means keep the stored figure** (S1): the screens send it only when the reader changed it in this edit, so a coach saving the target never writes back over the member’s newer figure the one they read. The save records who typed it (`apeAchievedTypedBy`).

caseSizeMinor.description: IDR sen per policy. Zero is refused — GOAL_INVALID_ASSUMPTION.

leadsToApptPct.description: *Appointment to Sales meeting*: per cent of set appointments that become a sales meeting.

closingRatePct.description: *Closing rate*: per cent of sales meetings that become a submitted policy.

period.description: Ignored: the period is the path. Accepted so a client may round-trip what it read.

monthsLeft.description: The divisor in force: the typed one, or the office’s calendar.

monthsLeftIsOverride.description: Whether `monthsLeft` was typed over (`true`) or is the office’s calendar.

achieved.description: The APE the plan is measured against: the newer of the typed figure and the office’s year to date (ADR-0230 §6) — a figure you type on your own plan is typed now, so it is the answer; on anybody else’s the figure typed while the office holds none, else the member’s stored one by the same rule.

projected.description: The cascade, as a save would store it. `null` when the inputs cannot make a plan — a save refuses that with `GOAL_INVALID_ASSUMPTION`.

apeAchievedMinor.description: IDR **sen**, whole: the APE produced so far this year, as the member estimates it — *perkiraan Anda*. `null` (or `0`) clears it (*Hapus*). The same figure Goal Settings shows as *APE yang sudah dicapai tahun ini* (ADR-0195).

sinceVersion.description: The version since which every published version’s limits exclude the value.

value.description: Money in IDR minor units; persistency in percent; the rest counts. **`null` is not zero** — it is *nothing uploaded*.

provenance.description: Which writer put it there. `null` when nothing has.

correction.description: A correction by hand — who, when, why — so a figure can say where it came from without a second request. A figure emptied by hand is `corrected` with a `null` value.

outOfBounds.description: A stored value outside its column’s current limits (AA UI-025): *Di luar batas sejak v<n>*. Flagged, never changed.

value.description: Money in IDR minor units; persistency in percent; the rest counts. **`null` is not zero** — it is *nothing uploaded*.

provenance.description: Which writer put it there. `null` when nothing has.

correction.description: A correction by hand — who, when, why — so a figure can say where it came from without a second request. A figure emptied by hand is `corrected` with a `null` value.

calculated.description: `true`: the sum of the months held from January (R4), never stored or typed; `false`: the year to date the file uploaded.

version.description: The template’s published version the header follows (R6).

header.description: `Agent Code`, `Agent Name`, each column `<label> (<unit>) [KODE]`, then `<label> YTD [KODE_YTD]` for each column whose year to date is uploaded.

file.description: The whole file. Names are quoted; a quote inside one is doubled (RFC 4180).

rowCount.description: How many active agents it lists.

label.description: The column’s name in the reader’s language.

header.description: The file’s header; `null` for a column the file lacks.

message.description: *Kolom <nama> kosong di file ini. Baris tetap diimpor.*, *Kolom <nama> tidak dipakai lagi*, …

correctionCells.description: Figures corrected by hand the file would change — each replaced only if ticked.

notInFile.description: Active members the file does not list. They keep what they have.

code.description: `UPLOAD_UNKNOWN_AGENT_CODE`, `UPLOAD_DUPLICATE_AGENT_CODE` or `UPLOAD_MALFORMED_CSV` for a row; `UPLOAD_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` for a cell, and `UPLOAD_LEADER_ONLY_VALUE` for *Unit Persistency (%)* on a row that is not an AB’s or an AAB’s (ADR-0201 §2).

message.description: Names the column in the header’s own words, and what is wrong.

kode.description: The cell’s kode; `null` for the row.

ytd.description: An uploaded year to date; `null` for the row.

replacedValue.description: The figure the correction replaced. The file carrying it again is how a re-upload of the old file looks.

ytd.description: A `ytd: upload` column’s year to date (`[KODE_YTD]`).

status.description: `not_provided` is a blank cell, and changes nothing — a file never clears a figure (ADR-0051).

before.description: Stored now. Money in IDR minor units.

after.description: What the file would write, in the same unit. `null` when not provided or refused.

raw.description: The cell as the file has it — money in *Rp M*.

correction.description: Set when the stored figure was corrected by hand and the file would change it. Replaced only if named in the commit’s `replace` (ADR-0053).

line.description: The file’s line, as a spreadsheet numbers it; the header is line 1.

name.description: The roster’s name. The file’s is never matched on.

codeRecovered.description: An all-digit code matched without its leading zeros, to the one member it fits (ADR-0052).

status.description: `held`: a code no member holds, kept as *Belum terdaftar* (ADR-0214 §8).

cells.description: One per `columns` entry, in its order; empty when the row is refused.

templateVersion.description: The template’s version the file was read against (R6).

format.description: A CSV, or an Excel workbook whose Data sheet was read (ADR-0184).

encoding.description: How a CSV’s bytes were read; `utf-8` for a workbook.

delimiter.description: A CSV’s delimiter; `,` for a workbook, whose numbers carry the point as their decimal mark.

revision.description: The month’s revision the preview was taken against. Confirm import sends it back.

columns.description: The columns read, in the template’s order.

notes.description: What the header says about the file’s columns (AA UI-013).

status.description: The history lists `committed`, `reverting` and `reverted`.

templateVersion.description: The template’s version the file was read against (R6): the history’s *v<n>*. 1 for a batch from before the template’s columns.

asOf.description: D8: the office day a running month’s upload stood at; `null` for a final one.

writtenRowCount.description: Rows with at least one figure written.

keptCellCount.description: Figures a revert kept, because something else wrote them since.

keptCorrectionCount.description: Corrections by hand the file would have changed, left as they were (ADR-0053).

replacedCorrectionCount.description: Corrections by hand replaced with the file’s figure, because the importer ticked them.

canRevert.description: Standing, and the month’s latest standing import — the only one revert takes.

revision.description: Advanced by every write to the month. A preview carries it; Confirm import must send it back unchanged, or is refused `VERSION_CONFLICT`.

locked.description: A locked month refuses import, revert and correction with `UPLOAD_MONTH_LOCKED` (ADR-0050).

reason.description: `open`/`schedule` follow the office’s window; `locked_by_hand`/`reopened` are somebody’s decision, which holds until the other is taken; `history` is a month of the required history never written, open until its first upload (ADR-0214 §11).

editableUntil.description: The last day the schedule leaves it open: month end plus `kpms.settings.productionLockGraceDays`, in the office’s calendar.

changedAt.description: When it was last locked or reopened by hand.

asOf.description: D8: the *as of* day of the month’s latest import while it ran; `null` for a final upload.

state.description: The month after the write, with its new revision.

changed.description: `false` when the figure already held that value — nothing was written, audited or advanced.

state.description: The month after the write, with its new revision.

membershipId.description: The membership, never a user id (invariant §2).

agentCode.description: The carrier-issued code the row is matched on.

values.description: This month’s figure per current column, by kode. A column not in force reads empty.

ytd.description: The year to date per column whose `ytd` is not `none`, by kode.

leader.description: A member of a leader class, `ab` or `aab` (ADR-0156): the rows a `rows: leaders` column is filled on.

monthlyActiveAgent.description: `MONTHLY_ACTIVE_AGENT` for the month (ADR-0054): `APE` or `POLICY_COUNT` above zero this month. **`null` is not `false`** — it is *not reported*: neither figure is positive and at least one is not held.

agentCode.description: The code, as ADR-0052 normalises it.

system.description: One of the four system columns (R1).

min.description: In the column’s unit (*Rp juta* for money).

inForce.description: `effectiveFrom` is on or before the month: before it the column reads *—*.

ytdMissingMonths.description: The months its year to date lacks (R4): *Belum lengkap · <Bul> belum diunggah*. Empty is complete.

templateId.description: The named template; `null` for the platform’s own configuration.

version.description: The published version the KPM reads now.

columns.description: The template’s current columns, in the file’s order.

historyFrom.description: The required history’s first month (R5): twelve before the KPM’s first.

firstMonth.description: The KPM’s first month on AgencyBoost (UI-150).

completePct.description: % of members filled for a month to be complete.

status.description: `UPLOAD_MONTH_COMPLETE`: never uploaded, below `completePct`, or complete.

members.description: Members on the month’s last day.

filled.description: Those of them filled in every column in force.

unregistered.description: *Belum terdaftar* rows (ADR-0214 §8), read-only, counted in nothing.

withData.description: Rows holding at least one figure. Zero means nothing uploaded yet.

config.description: The template the columns follow (ADR-0214 §14), read live — the banner’s *Kolom mengikuti <template> v<n>.*

completeness.description: This month, as complete or not (`UPLOAD_MONTH_COMPLETE`).

ytdMissingMonths.description: The months any year to date lacks: *YTD belum lengkap: <Bul> <tahun> belum diunggah.*

months.description: From `config.historyFrom` to the current month, each as complete or not.

companyId.description: From GET /companies. With `inviteToken`, the invite’s office’s insurer is used, whatever this says.

agentCode.description: With `inviteToken`, the invite’s agent code is used, whatever this says.

inviteToken.description: The token from an invite link, `/register?invite=…`.

dateOfBirth.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`. In the past, and at least 18 years ago.

companyJoinMonth.description: `YYYY-MM`: the month they joined the insurer chosen in `companyId` (*Joined Prudential*). Not in the future.

workStatus.description: Copied onto the membership they are given when an office takes them on (ADR-0158 §1).

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

refreshToken.description: Only for non-browser clients. A browser sends the httpOnly cookie set at login and should omit this entirely.

token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Expires in 15 minutes.

currentPassword.description: The password the account signs in with now.

preferredName.description: What colleagues call you. Empty, blank or `null` means none: it is stored as `null`, and your full name is shown wherever a name is.

pronoun.description: Yours to set. It appears in the coaching commitment sentence your leader reads.

dateOfBirth.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`. In the past, and at least 18 years ago.

companyJoinMonth.description: `YYYY-MM`: the month you joined your insurer. Not in the future.

workStatus.description: Written on your membership in your office; on your account until you have one.

locale.description: The language you read AgencyBoost in: `id`, Bahasa Indonesia, or `en`, English. Saved on your account, so it follows you to every device. Not clearable: anything else, `null` included, is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`.

phone.description: Your WhatsApp number. Spaces, dashes, dots and brackets go, and a leading `+62`, `62` or `0`; what is left must be 9 to 13 digits, stored as `+62…`, else `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming `phone`. Empty, blank or `null` clears it.

email.description: The address of the other login to link.

currentPassword.description: The password the caller signs in with now.

token.description: The token from the link sent to the other login's address.

password.description: The password of the login the link was sent to.

userId.description: The linked login to switch to: `linkedLogin.userId` on `GET /auth/me`.

password.description: That login's password — only after `409 AUTH_LINK_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`, when this browser holds no live session of it.

mimeType.description: The crop is always a JPEG.

bytes.description: What the browser is about to send: at most 512 KB (`AVATAR.MAX_BYTES`), checked here and again against what storage holds (ADR-0040).

kind.description: `template`: one of the company’s active templates, named by `templateId` — or, with `templateLibrary`, one of the Template library’s, *Template · Default template*, which holds the AgencyBoost defaults. `empty`: nothing but the three cascade activity types. `defaults` is refused 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, `details.field: startFrom.kind` (ADR-0168 §2).

templateId.description: Required when `kind` is `template`, unless `templateLibrary` is true: then it names one of the Template library’s active templates, and absent its default.

templateLibrary.description: With `kind: template`, the template is the Template library’s rather than the company’s — *Template · Default template*. Its settings are copied across companies, and every role they name must be on the company’s ladder (409 TEMPLATE_RUNG_UNKNOWN).

code.description: Unique within the company.

companyId.description: The company the office is for, when the Super Admin corrects it on the card (ADR-0191 §2). Absent, the request's. The applicant must belong to it: `409 TENANT_COMPANY_MISMATCH` otherwise, before anything is written.

startFrom.description: *Mulai dari* (ADR-0213 §3): what the office starts from, offered on the card when the company has **no template** yet — a built-in template (`{ kind: "template", templateLibrary: true, templateId? }`) or *Kosong* (`{ kind: "empty" }`). Absent: the company's default template, or the built-in default where it has none. `defaults` is refused `400`, as on `POST /admin/tenants`.

reason.example: This branch already trades under KPM 0417.
reason.description: Kept, and sent back to whoever asked. A refusal with nothing to act on is not an answer.

slug.description: Derived from the name by the console and editable there. Unique among companies that have not been deleted; a clash is refused with COMPANY_SLUG_TAKEN.

usesPlatformDefaults.description: True copies the Template library: its role ladder with the leader tiers, product catalog, carrier rules and recruitment playbook, and its Default template — activity taxonomy, ratios, lead ladders, training tree, activation checklist, capability ladder and event types — as the company's first, default template. A copy: changing the Template later changes no company made from it. Where no Template library exists, the AgencyBoost defaults. False leaves every one of them empty, for a company whose presets are being authored from scratch. The role ladder is seeded either way: an office whose company has none is one nobody can join.

slug.description: Changeable: nothing stores it. Every office points at the company by id, and the slug is a label. A clash is refused with COMPANY_SLUG_TAKEN.

code.description: Stable and semantic. Upper-cased on the way in, and never changed afterwards.

displayOrder.description: Junior first. Presentation only — nothing references it.

leaderTier.description: *Senior Leader* (what AB is), *Associate Leader* (what AAB is), or `null` — *Not a leader*. A member’s role class is derived from it wherever they are placed on the rung (ADR-0156). Absent is `null`.

*Senior Leader* (what AB is), *Associate Leader* (what AAB is), or `null` — *Not a leader*. A member’s role class is derived from it wherever they are placed on the rung (ADR-0156). Refused `409 ORG_LEVEL_TIER_IN_USE` while anybody holds the rung.

status.description: Archiving retires a rung without deleting it. Nothing is ever deleted here.

expectedVersion.description: The rung's `version` as read, `0` for a rung never changed. A rung changed since is refused `409 VERSION_CONFLICT` with `details.expectedVersion` and `details.actualVersion`, and nothing is written. Absent, unchecked.

phone.description: Their WhatsApp number — **stored and shown, never a channel**: nothing is sent by WhatsApp or SMS (ADR-0212 §4). Spaces, dashes, dots and brackets go, and a leading `+62`, `62` or `0`; what is left must be 9 to 13 digits, stored as `+62…`, else `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming `owner.phone`.

email.description: Where the invitation goes. An existing account with it becomes the Owner (its company, an agent code and a verified address required, ADR-0191 §5); with none, an account is made for it with no usable password. Absent: no account, the Owner waits named (`pendingOwner`).

agentCode.description: *Kode agen pemilik*: their code at the insurer. Required to make a new account (the Owner is the KPM’s root AB under it); an existing account keeps its own.

code.description: Unique within the company. Prefixes agent codes.

timezone.description: v1 runs on a single time zone. Asia/Jakarta is the only accepted value; omit it and the office inherits the same value from its company (ADR-0016).

startFrom.description: What the office is built from. Absent: the company’s default template. A kind the source holds none of is empty in the office; every office has the three cascade activity types.

owner.description: ***Pemilik KPM*** (ADR-0212 §1): made the KPM’s Owner as one unit with it — a refusal of the Owner leaves no KPM. Absent (*"Lewati, nanti saja"*): a KPM with no Owner, under *Perlu perhatian Anda*.

sendInvitation.description: *"Kirim undangan … sekarang"*: email the Owner a one-time link to choose a password, alive for `ROSTER_INVITATION.TTL_DAYS`. Only an Owner with an account who has never signed in is sent one.

payload.description: The whole payload for this kind. Shape depends on the kind: `activity_taxonomy` is `{ categories, types }` — a category may carry `summaryGroupCode` and `summaryGroupLabel`, both or neither (ADR-0064) — `lead_pipeline` is `{ statuses }`, `ratio_set` is `{ ratios }`.

expectedRevision.description: The `revision` of what the editor opened — the draft, else the newest published, else `0` for nothing. Somebody else saved or published since: `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`, `details.expectedRevision` and `details.actualRevision`, nothing written. Absent, the save lands whatever the revision.

email.description: The account to make Owner. It must already exist — create one at /register or with POST /auth/register. Email is what a Super Admin normally knows.

userId.description: Alternative to email, for when you already have the id.

owner.description: *Ganti pemilik* to somebody named here (ADR-0212 §3): `owner.email` required. An account with it is made the Owner under the same refusals; with none, an account is made for it and the Owner invited. Instead of `email`/`userId`.

sendInvitation.description: With `owner`: email the new Owner their invitation (an account that has signed in is sent none).

companyId.description: The insurer the office moves to.

startDate.description: The first day, an office date (YYYY-MM-DD in the office's timezone). Null with endDate for no dates.

endDate.description: The last day the office can be used, an office date. From 00:00 the next office day every member is refused TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED unless keepActiveAfterEnd is on. On or after startDate.

pricePerLeaderMinor.description: Price per leader per month, in IDR minor units (sen), whole rupiah. Informational: nothing is charged from it.

maxLeaders.description: The most leaders (active ABs and AABs, the Owner included) the office may have. Null for no limit. May be set below the leaders it has now: nobody is demoted, new ones are refused.

keepActiveAfterEnd.description: On, and the office stays open after its end date (Ended — kept active). Never null.

plan.description: *Paket* (ADR-0211 §1): `six_months` (*6 bulan*) or `annual` (*Tahunan*), a label — nothing renews or is charged from it. `null` clears it; **absent keeps the plan the office has**, so a client sending the five fields alone changes no plan. Audited with the other fields.

rows.description: The rows, as text. Tab-separated from a spreadsheet paste, or comma-separated. The header row is optional. A file is sent to `roster/file/preview` and `roster/file`.
The rows, as text. Tab-separated from a spreadsheet paste, or comma-separated. The header row is optional. A file is sent to `roster/file/preview` and `roster/file`.

invite.description: Mail each new person a one-time link to choose their password (email only, ADR-0010). Default `true`.

reason.description: Recorded in the audit log. Required.

purpose.description: **A session only looks** (ADR-0206 §3): `support`, or left out. `setup` is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `details.field: 'purpose'`, and nothing is written — the setup session is retired. Any other value is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `details.violations`.

rungMap.description: Optional (ADR-0213 §4): a rung the copy names that the ladder lacks, to one of its active rungs. Within one company the ladder is shared, so it is rarely needed; a target that is not an active rung is `400`.

from.description: `empty`: nothing in any of the seven kinds — an office made from it starts empty but for the three cascade activity types. `defaults`: each kind a published version 1 of the AgencyBoost defaults. `{ templateId }`: **a copy** of one of this company’s templates — each kind’s newest published version as the copy’s version 1, drafts not copied, codes kept, training files referenced, the recruitment playbook with them (ADR-0210 §1). A company’s first template becomes its default (ADR-0213 §3).

fromCompanyId.description: The company the template is imported from: not this one.

rungMap.description: *Salin dari…*’s rung map (ADR-0213 §4, B1-7): each rung the source names and this company’s ladder lacks, to one of its **active** rungs. Every configuration naming a mapped rung is rewritten to the mapped code, duplicates merged, and the audit row records the map. A rung left unmapped is still `409 TEMPLATE_RUNG_UNKNOWN` naming it; a target that is not an active rung is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming it; an entry for a rung the ladder has is ignored.

isDefault.description: `true` makes this the company’s default, moving it from the template that was. `false` is refused on the default (409 TEMPLATE_IS_DEFAULT): a company always has one, so another is made the default instead.

kinds.description: The sections to apply, each its newest published version. Applied in *Terbitkan semua*’s order, whatever order they are sent in.

kpmIds.description: The KPMs to apply them to, each one made from this template. Any other is `404`, and nothing is written.

replaceChanged.description: The second confirmation: KPMs whose own changes may be replaced. A KPM the server finds *changed by the KPM* and not listed here is refused `TEMPLATE_APPLY_UNCONFIRMED`, and nothing is written for it.

mimeType.description: A module’s *File* or *Video*: an HTML lesson (`text/html`) among them (ADR-0217 §1), confirmed by its first bytes and drawn only in a sandboxed frame. Any other type is a `400`.

bytes.description: What the browser is about to send. Checked here so an oversized file is refused before it is uploaded, and checked again against what storage reports (ADR-0040).

files.description: `{ id?, label, storageKey, mimeType, bytes }` per file, each a confirmed upload of this company.

videos.description: Short videos (`.mp4`), the same shape. Anything longer than the ceiling is a link.

links.description: `{ id?, label, url }` per link, `https` only.

expectedRevision.description: The `revision` of the section’s draft the editor read. Somebody else saved or published since: `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`, nothing written.

companyId.description: The company the template is made in: the office’s own, or another.

toRole.description: The rung, by its code on the company’s ladder, in any case: `ab`, `aab`, `agent`, or a rung the company added. What the member is given — AB, AAB or Agent rights — follows the rung’s leader tier. A code that is no active rung is refused `409 ORG_LEVEL_NOT_ON_LADDER`.

reason.description: Kept in the role change log, which is the only place this can be read back.

action.description: `promote`: the role change the limit refused, onto the rung named. `activate`: letting in a pending member who stands on a leader rung — approving their join request, or tagging them into your unit.

orgLevelCode.description: For `promote`: the rung, by its code on the company’s ladder.

reason.example: Ready to bring on their own agents
reason.description: For `promote`: kept in the role change log when AgencyBoost approves it.

action.description: Where the reports of the person being removed go. There is no default: leaving it to the server would be a silent reorganisation of somebody else’s unit.

toMembershipId.description: Required when action is `reassign`. The membership their reports move to.

confirmation.description: The literal word REMOVE, trimmed and case-insensitive. Checked here as well as in the screen — a confirmation only the screen enforces is not a confirmation.

reason.description: Kept on the removal history event, and sent to them.

subtree.description: Required when they still have direct reports; refused otherwise.

ownerMembershipId.description: The membership that owns it. Never a name — the prototype stores `ownerName`, which breaks the moment anybody is renamed or two people share one.

groupIds.description: Every live group this person should be in. Absent ids are removed; tags on retired groups are kept, because they are the record that a cohort existed.

isCoreLeader.description: Core Leader (ADR-0159): who, besides the Owner and the Admins, opens and writes in the Strategic Leader Forum’s meetings and reads the office’s KPM analytics. A leader’s only: setting it on a member whose rung is not a leader rung is refused `400 CORE_LEADER_NOT_A_LEADER`, and changing it needs `member:tag_core_leader`. It grants no hierarchy.
Tag (`true`) or untag (`false`) this member *Core Leader*. Their groups are untouched. Setting it on a member whose rung is not a leader rung is refused `400 CORE_LEADER_NOT_A_LEADER`.

phone.description: Spaces, dashes, dots and brackets go, and a leading `+62`, `62` or `0`; what is left must be 9 to 13 digits, stored as `+62…`, else `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming `phone`.

routeToMembershipId.description: One of your own AABs, from GET /join/requests/routing. Omitted adds them to your own unit. Ignored for an AB or AAB requester — a leader is not placed in a unit, they are tagged to you directly.

joinDate.description: The day they joined, an office date: the office’s today at the latest, and not before 1980 — an existing agent may have joined years ago. Omitted, the office’s today. Ignored for somebody who already has a join date in this office.

fields.description: The exact form fields storage needs beside `file`, every one sent as it is and **before** `file`, which goes last — the browser need not know which they are. collection.description: Where the record is: a lead, a coaching session, or a month of the production file (`monthlyAgentData`).

shortLabel.description: *Nama singkat* (ADR-0229 §5): the one line the Unit Dashboard’s activity table shows, the full `label` on tap. `null` for none.

appliesToOrgLevelCodes.description: The rungs that may log this, **inherited from its category and never stored here**. Empty means every rung.

numerator.description: Activity type codes, summed. Never the prototype's item numbers.

origin.description: `platform` rows were provisioned — their numerator and denominator are fixed so that two offices’ figures mean the same thing. `office` rows are the office’s own and free in every respect.

appliesToOrgLevelCodes.description: Ladder rung codes. **Empty means every rung.**

standardNumerator.description: The formula this office was provisioned with (ADR-0024), or `null` on a ratio it created. What a divergence is measured against, and what the screen shows an Owner they moved away from.

divergesFromStandard.description: The formula no longer matches what this office was seeded from (ADR-0024). A display and support caveat: nothing is excluded from any comparison on account of it, because a platform comparison computes the seeded formula rather than reading this row.

displayUnit.description: How to write `benchmark` for a reader. `percent`: × 100, as typed (15%, 15,5%; ADR-0174 §2). `decimal`: two decimals (0,30). `points`: ± percentage points (±30 points). Always `points` on a `band` ratio.

code.description: What every lead holds. Renaming the label leaves this alone.

isTerminal.description: The stage that closes this pipeline, and what gates marking a lead successful. Exactly one per pipeline — a property, not "the last one in the list".

isLateStage.description: A stage the lead is expected to convert from this period, and what the KPM Overview counts as *Expected to close*. Unlike the terminal flag it is not exclusive, and it is never true on the stage that closes the pipeline.

code.description: The identity. Never changes, never reused.

skillCode.description: The skill it teaches. **Its category is that skill's**, never stored here.

description.description: *Deskripsi singkat* (ADR-0220 §1): the grey line under the name, plain text, or `null`.

material.description: The settings list only: where the material agents are shown comes from — `own`, the office's replacement; `company`, the template's; `none`, no file, video or link. What *x / y modul punya materi* counts.

An AB two layers down the office is *Layer 1* of their own tree, because AC-1 says layer one is you. Computing it here keeps one coordinate frame: a client that subtracted its own root's depth would be a second one, and the two disagree the moment a projection has roots at different depths.

canTagCoreLeader.description: Whether this viewer may tag or untag this member *Core Leader* from the row: they hold `member:tag_core_leader`, and the member stands on a leader rung and has not left (ADR-0159 §1). An offer, never the gate: `PUT /members/:id/core-leader` refuses regardless.

joinedAt.description: The system’s stamp: the instant the membership was made active.

cursor.description: The cursor this page was asked with; null for the first.

nextCursor.description: Ask with this for the next page (*Muat lagi*); null on the last.

limit.description: The most groups a page holds.

name.description: Their name, or null if the account is gone.

actionLabels.description: Each of `actions`, in the same order, with its label in the reader's words — what the chip shows.

actors.description: The actors of a leader note’s rows are left out (ADR-0073).

facets.description: On the first page only (no `cursor`); null on every later one.

expiresAt.description: Time-boxed. The session cannot outlive this.

sessionId.description: The session's id, named on its `impersonation.started` audit entry.

readOnly.description: Always `true`: a session only looks (ADR-0206 §3). Every write in it is `403 IMPERSONATION_READ_ONLY`.

code.description: The tier’s stable code. A tier is named by it, never by its position.

minLeaders.description: The smallest leader count the tier prices, inclusive.

maxLeaders.description: The largest leader count the tier prices, inclusive; `null` for the open last tier.

standardMinor.description: The standard rate per leader per month, in IDR minor units (sen). Shown struck through.

sixMonthMinor.description: The six-month rate per leader per month, in IDR minor units (sen).

annualMinor.description: The annual rate per leader per month, in IDR minor units (sen): the six-month rate less `annualDiscountPct` percent, exactly.

customPricing.description: Shown publicly as “Custom pricing”: its card draws no rate.

tiers.description: Smallest leader count first. Together they cover every count from 1 up, without a gap.

annualDiscountPct.description: The annual rate’s discount off the six-month rate, in percent.

members.description: On an office’s row, its active memberships now. On a company’s and the platform’s, the **people**: distinct accounts among those memberships, so somebody in two offices counts once there.

byRung.description: Active memberships by rung of the company’s ladder, senior first — on every row the offices’ sum.

joinedThisMonth.description: Memberships that began this calendar month — on every row the offices’ sum.

leftThisMonth.description: Memberships removed this calendar month — on every row the offices’ sum.

signedIn7d.description: Of `members`, who signed in within the last 7 days: memberships on an office’s row, accounts on a company’s and the platform’s.

signedIn30d.description: The same, within the last 30 days.

kind.description: `figure` a value; `pending` *pending data* — no source holds it for its period, never 0; `none` *—*, a ratio over nothing; `blocked` *Not tracked*, a row the table leaves empty in this column; `unrecorded` *—*, a column or a row a scorecard kept before it existed does not hold — never computed for it; `not_uploaded` *—*, *Not uploaded yet*: a *Full Year* or *YTD* column of last year with no month of its period uploaded.

value.description: On a `figure`: exact — IDR minor units, a count, a ratio or a whole percentage.

leavesOut.description: On a `figure`: the months of its period, `YYYY-MM`, not uploaded yet.
